MARKET.head: Liv-ex upgrades LWIN matching with AI and bulk price enrichment
MARKET.summ: Liv-ex has introduced two connected improvements designed to help members work with wine lists more efficiently and at scale
takeaways: Liv-ex has added Wine Matcher to List Studio, letting members match wine lists to LWIN and enrich them with trusted data.
The redesigned matching engine combines modern AI with Liv-ex's proprietary wine data, keeping precision above 99%.
The engine processes up to 1,500 lines per minute and handles lists of up to 10,000 lines.

MARKET.head: Bordeaux to host VINITECH-SIFEL trade show with 700 exhibitors in December 2026
MARKET.summ: From 1-3 December 2026, Bordeaux will welcome wine professionals from around the world for VINITECH-SIFEL, a leading international trade show dedicated to innovation and solutions for the wine, fruit and vegetable sectors. Bringing together 700 exhibitors, 40,000 professionals from 70 countries and 70,000 m² of exhibition...
takeaways: VINITECH-SIFEL, a trade show for wine, fruit and vegetable sectors, runs in Bordeaux from 1 to 3 December 2026.
The event expects 700 exhibitors and 40,000 professionals from 70 countries across 70,000 m² of space.
International buyers with equipment investment plans may qualify for hotel accommodation and travel support through the International Buyers Program.

MARKET.head: Vinitaly.USA moves to New York with 300 exhibitors in October 2026
MARKET.summ: The Italian wine trade event makes its New York City debut October 26 and 27, bringing 300 exhibitors and 2,500 wines to Pier 36
takeaways: Vinitaly.USA, organized by Veronafiere with the Italian Trade Agency, debuts in New York on October 26 and 27, 2026.
Pier 36 will host 300 exhibitors presenting 2,500 labels, the largest exhibitor count yet, after two years in Chicago.
A 95-winery delegation organized by the Italian Trade Agency joins regional collectives from Friuli-Venezia Giulia, Lazio and Sardinia.

MARKET.head: Global wine demand shifts from red toward white and sparkling styles
MARKET.summ: The global wine industry has been undergoing a significant structural transformation. While declining overall wine consumption has attracted considerable attention, another important trend has emerged beneath the surface: a steady shift in consumer demand from red wine towards white and sparkling wine.
takeaways: IWSR data shows red wine's share of global consumption fell from about 52% in 2012 to 43% in 2025.
Over the same period white wine rose from 31% to 34%, and sparkling wine from 8% to 13%.
Red wine has lost ground as consumers grow more selective, moderate intake and choose drinks by occasion.

MARKET.head: France's 2026 wine harvest set to fall 14% below recent average
MARKET.summ:
This year’s harvest expected to be down 2% on mediocre yield in 2025, when production was lowest in nearly 70 years

France’s wine industry is facing a historic low harvest after the country was hit by a series of summer heatwaves.

At about 35m hectolitres, the total harvest would be down 2% on a mediocre 2025...
takeaways: French agriculture ministry estimates 2026 harvest at about 35 million hectolitres, down 2% on 2025 and 14% below the 2021-2025 average.
Champagne harvest finished in September for the first time, with production halved from last year and the five-year average.
Burgundy and Beaujolais output is projected 30% below the five-year average, while Bordeaux is expected to rise 10% on 2025.

MARKET.head: Seven proposed US wine regions await TTB approval for new AVA status
MARKET.summ: From Minnesota to New Jersey, seven proposed AVAs aim to distinguish emerging regions by climate, soils, and grape varieties
takeaways: Seven potential new American Viticultural Areas are in early stages, each needing years of Alcohol and Tobacco Tax and Trade Bureau approval.
The proposed Annapolis-Sea Ranch AVA would cover 26,637 acres with 651 acres of grapes across a dozen vineyards in Sonoma County.
The proposed 723,760-acre Deschutes River AVA would be the first recognized winegrowing region in central Oregon.

MARKET.head: VinePair's weekly roundup flags Uncle Nearest sale talks and other drinks-industry updates
MARKET.summ: This is VinePair’s Booze News Weekly Roundup, where we gather the hottest headlines and product releases every Friday for a snapshot of what’s happening in the beverage alcohol industry. This week, we have updates on Uncle Nearest’s potential buyers, Mark Zuckerberg’s Guinness flop, the latest product releases, and more.
takeaways: Uncle Nearest's potential buyers are covered in this week's VinePair Booze News roundup.
Roundup also covers Mark Zuckerberg's Guinness flop and the latest beverage alcohol product releases.

CULTURE.head: Yinchuan hosts first Asian OIV World Congress of Vine and Wine
CULTURE.summ: China hosted the 47th OIV World Congress of Vine and Wine, marking a historic first for Asia
takeaways: China hosted the 47th OIV World Congress of Vine and Wine in Yinchuan, Ningxia, from 12 to 16 October 2026.
It was the first OIV World Congress held in Asia, drawing over 600 participants from 47 countries.
The congress featured 420 scientific contributions and six technical visits, with presentations to be published open-access.

CULTURE.head: Oregon's AAPI Food & Wine Festival Named Next Wave Nonprofit of the Year
CULTURE.summ: In 2020, Lois and Dave Cho became the first Korean American winemakers in Oregon when they launched CHO Wines in the Willamette Valley. The fast-growing winery quickly amassed a following and received critical acclaim, but they kept fielding the same question: “What informs your palate for wine?” The answer to that question...
takeaways: AAPI Food & Wine, founded by Lois and Dave Cho of CHO Wines, won Next Wave Awards' Nonprofit of the Year.
The festival launched in 2023 in Oregon's Willamette Valley, featuring Asian American-owned wineries and Portland chefs.
It has since expanded to New York City, with a March residency partnering with Korean restaurant Atoboy.

CULTURE.head: Cloudy and unfiltered wines gain ground, with Marks & Spencer and Tesco stocking pét nats
CULTURE.summ:
There’s something refreshing about unfiltered or unfined wines. We filter through a selection …

Centuries ago, Geoffrey Chaucer observed that “ther is no newe gyse that it nas old”. This truth - that there is nothing new under the sun - certainly applies to wine: every year, a well-documented or ancient viticultural...
takeaways: Pét nat is an ancestral method of bottling before fermentation finishes, typically left undisgorged and therefore cloudy.
Zainab Majerikova, head of wine for the Ottolenghi group, says cloudy wines have texture and suit food with complex flavours.

CULTURE.head: European bartenders say American visitors are curious, though many still order vodka Martinis
CULTURE.summ: Over decades of regular trips to Europe, Regine Rousseau, the Chicago-based founder of wine marketing and events consultancy Shall We Wine, never really subscribed to the directive often preached by U.S. travel publications: When traveling abroad, try not to let your American show. “Number one: I like wearing really bright...
takeaways: Giorgio Bargiani, assistant director of mixology at The Connaught Bar in London, says American bar guests are entertaining and genuinely curious.
Connaught Bar makes about 30,000 Martinis a year, and American guests often request vodka instead of gin.
Europe saw a record 24 million American trips in 2025, with another 5 percent rise expected this year, per The Wall Street Journal.

SCIENCE.head: Brazilian tropical reds keep polyphenols and health-relevant compounds through 12 months of storage
SCIENCE.summ: Young varietal and experimental wines from Vitis vinifera - Petit Verdot, Tempranillo, and Syrah - cultivated in a tropical semiarid region (Northeast Brazil) were evaluated with regard to their phenolic composition and chromatic characteristics during a storage period of 12-month
takeaways: Researchers from Brazilian universities and Embrapa tested young Petit Verdot, Tempranillo and Syrah wines from the São Francisco Valley over 12 months of bottle storage.
Petit Verdot showed less colour change than wines from temperate climates, and polyphenols declined in line with the usual storage pattern.
Anthocyanin and trans-resveratrol levels stayed above published literature values, while the red wines softened in flavour and all wines lost some sensory character.

SCIENCE.head: Tropical Brazilian, Indian, Thai and Venezuelan wineries now produce quality wine at scale
SCIENCE.summ: A lot of grapes are produced in the tropics, but only a little part is used to winemaking, what represents some million liters of tropical wines produced per year. The present industry of tropical wine production began 30 years ago
takeaways: Tropical wine production began about 30 years ago and now has commercial wineries in Brazil, India, Thailand and Venezuela.
Brazilian researchers at Embrapa grew Petit Verdot, Tempranillo and Syrah in Northeast Brazil's tropical semiarid region, testing phenolic composition over 12 months.
The analysis predicts high-quality tropical wine in expressive volumes, despite marketing challenges and know-how gaps in tropical viticulture.

SCIENCE.head: Heat treatments shift grapevine fruit set differently across four cultivars
SCIENCE.summ: In the 2009/2010 growing season undervine tents (a passive, open system) were used to increase daytime temperature by 3-5 oC over ambient during the growing season. Four grapevine cultivars (Cabernet Franc, Chardonnay, Semillon and Shiraz) were assessed for reproductive performance under these conditions
takeaways: In 2009/2010, Australian researchers at the University of Adelaide raised daytime vineyard temperatures 3-5 degrees Celsius using undervine tents.
Chardonnay under heat set less fruit, producing fewer berries and lighter bunches, while Semillon and Shiraz set more fruit.
Cabernet Franc showed no significant differences between heated and ambient treatments.

SCIENCE.head: Rootstock study finds 110 Richter grows most roots under low water
SCIENCE.summ: Grapevine is a landscape forming crop which, due to the quality and taste demanded by consumers, as well as the different agronomical practices, could be vulnerable to global change effects
takeaways: Researchers grew Grenache grafted onto three rootstocks, 110 Richter, 41-B and 161-49, in rhizotrons under two water regimes.
110 Richter developed greater root length than the other two rootstocks, though this did not translate into more vegetative growth.
Root growth peaked in summer during berry growth and ripening, with continuous root turnover even after ripening.

SCIENCE.head: Part Two of vineyard lab series examines how irrigation water shapes mineral nutrients
SCIENCE.summ: THURSDAY, OCTOBER 8, 2026. BY STAN GRANT, VITICULTURIST. Part Two of a Three-Part Vineyard Mineral Nutrient Management Lab Analysis Series.
takeaways: Viticulturist Stan Grant's Part Two of a three-part series covers evaluating lab analyses of vineyard irrigation water.
Nearly pure irrigation water, like Sierra Nevada snowmelt, strips minerals from soils, making them less fertile and more acidic.
Saline well water can make drip-irrigated soils saline, forcing vines to work harder to take up water.

SCIENCE.head: Newsletter reports cover crop and mulching research in vineyard soils and microbes
SCIENCE.summ: Our September newsletter is out. This month: Tasting Climate Change 2026 sessions now available to watch; practical guides on cover crops, weed management and compost teas; fresh research on resilience and economics in regenerative vineyards from France to Sonoma, plus new recognition for ROC and regenerative producers from...
takeaways: A 2026 Italian study in Environmental Microbiome found cover-crop under-vine mulching raised microbial diversity in a non-irrigated northern Italian vineyard.
The same study reported improved soil conditions and reduced pathogen pressure under the cover-crop mulch treatment.
A 2026 Field Crops Research study of Mediterranean rainfed vineyards found roller-crimped cover crops improved soil cover and vine water status.

SCIENCE.head: SFI 2026 offers UK vineyards payments for cover crops and habitat actions
SCIENCE.summ: The second application window for the Sustainable Farming Incentive (SFI) is set to open on 22 September, so Hutchinsons head of environmental services, Georgina Wallis, highlights some actions that may be of interest to growers in the viticulture sector. While the SFI is primarily aimed at arable and livestock farms, vines and...
takeaways: Vines and horticultural permanent crops are included within the SFI 2026 scheme, which offers 71 actions, several relevant to vineyards.
LEAF Marque Standard version 17.0 requires 5% or more of farm or site area managed as habitat, with an optional 10% target.
Overwinter cover crop (CSAM2) should be sown by late August or early September, though SFI allows up to 12 months to establish mixes.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Santuvario, a natural wine producer in Alto Piemonte, Italy
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Santuvario is a small natural wine producer based in the town of Borgomanero in Alto Piemonte, at the foot of
NEWSLETTERS.author: Jamie Goode
takeaways: Santuvario is a small natural wine producer in Borgomanero, Alto Piemonte, run by Ivano Barbaglia and Paola Fornara, who began making wine in 2012.
The author tasted Santuvario wines at VinNatur in Paris in November 2025, scoring the Lazio 2022 94/100 and the Gino Bianco 2022 93/100.

NEWSLETTERS.summ: A mysterious artifact behind the winery at Mateus Nicolau de Almeida in the Douro Superior region, with a hillside of
NEWSLETTERS.author: Alder Yarrow
takeaways: Vinography's image post features a mysterious artifact behind the winery at Mateus Nicolau de Almeida in Portugal's Douro Superior region.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Pairing Wine With Fall
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Wines to pour with autumnal fare, plus this week’s favorite stories about food, wine, and culture
NEWSLETTERS.author: Meg Maker
takeaways: Meg Maker's piece argues autumnal foods are cooked, cured, pickled, smoked or dried, transformed into something more complex than their original state.
She says fall flavors in northern New England lean toward the dark end of the spectrum, contrasting with summer's brights.

NEWSLETTERS.head: A Level Playing Field
NEWSLETTERS.summ: What do we mean by the word “Burgundian”? Used indiscriminately to describe a region that is famously, almost defiantly complex, it’s a term that covers so many appellations, terroirs and styles as to be almost meaningless, especially when it comes to white Burgundy. Are we talking Chablis, the Côte Beaune or the Mâconnais?
NEWSLETTERS.author: Tim Atkin MW
takeaways: Tim Atkin reports a blind tasting of 24 Chardonnays, 10 from Pyramid Valley and Smith & Sheth and 14 from Burgundy, organised by Steve Smith MW.

Atkin says New Zealand Chardonnays topped two of four categories and should have won a third, with the 2024 Smith & Sheth Onewa Chardonnay narrowly losing to Domaine Guffens-Heynen's 2023 Saint Véran Clos de Poncetys.
Atkin argues top Chardonnay is now a level playing field, citing Burgundy's warmer climate and Domaine Leflaive finishing picking on August 18th this year.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Cabernet Franc in the Press: October 2026
NEWSLETTERS.summ: From Livermore to the Loire: Cabernet Franc in Food & Wine, Robb Report, Le Point, JancisRobinson.com, and more
NEWSLETTERS.author: Cab Franc Chronicles
takeaways: Only 3,501 acres of Cabernet Franc were planted in California in 2025, versus 90,040 acres of Cabernet Sauvignon, per the California Grape Acreage Report.
In February 2025, the Livermore Valley officially named Cabernet Franc and Sauvignon Blanc as its signature red and white varieties.
Lang & Reed, founded by John and Tracey Skupny in 1996 to make only Cabernet Franc, was profiled by Alder Yarrow in Jancis Robinson's site.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Telling a mountain to move
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Delving into the details of change in the DO Montsant wine region of Catalunya
NEWSLETTERS.author: Miquel Hudin
takeaways: DO Montsant, in Catalunya's Priorat area, has revised its bylaws to certify vi brisat (orange-style) wines and create a classification for minimal-intervention wines.
The minimal-intervention classification requires mandatory hand-harvesting, organic certification, spontaneous fermentations, and no oenological additives except gentle filtration.
The author says the Montsant changes arrive late, noting the orange wine market is collapsing, and that the DO did not reply to questions about its maximum SO2 limit.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Most Burgundy Wine Buyers Are Still Shopping Backwards in 2026. Here’s the Strategy Négociants Hope You Never Learn
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Learn the strategy Burgundy wine négociants hope you never discover to find the best winery deals in 2026
NEWSLETTERS.author: Jonathan Finch
takeaways: Louis Latour, Louis Jadot, Maison Albert Bichot and Bouchard Père & Fils are named as leading négociant houses dominating Burgundy sales worldwide.
Capitain-Gagnerot Corton-Charlemagne is priced at a fraction of Coche-Dury's, though grown only a few rows away from it.

And you’ll […] This article was...
NEWSLETTERS.author: Joe Roberts
takeaways: The author notes growing amusement at repeatedly searching whether a Vintage Port has already been featured on the site.

NEWSLETTERS.head: 400 Montepulciano Bottles for Thomas Jefferson circa 1805
NEWSLETTERS.summ: The wine everyone’s been gushing over since the middle ages!
NEWSLETTERS.author: Eveline Chartier
takeaways: A 1350 trade contract between the Del Pecora family and merchant Jacopo di Vanni is the oldest known document for Vino Nobile di Montepulciano, held in Florence's State Archives.
A 2024 document from the Jesuit archives in Montepulciano shows the term Vino Nobile was used in 1766, earlier than the previously known 1787 reference.
Thomas Jefferson received 473 bottles of Montepulciano in November 1805 and requested 400 bottles annually from Thomas Appleton in April 1806.

NEWSLETTERS.head: The Encyclopedia of Wine - Fresh Take or Same Same?
NEWSLETTERS.summ: I take a look at a brand new reference work to see how it stacks up with the competition
NEWSLETTERS.author: Simon J. Woolf
takeaways: Dorling Kindersley's The Encyclopedia of Wine is published 8 October in the UK and 10 November in the US.
Editor-in-chief David Williams aims for an authoritative but accessible reference, written by 28 acknowledged experts such as Jane Anson and Wink Lorch.
The 400-page book is positioned as a less stuffy rival to The Oxford Companion to Wine and The World Atlas of Wine.
